why: Repeatedly pairing the highest with the lowest remaining developer is exactly the sorted-array two-pointer walk: sort, then pair arr[i] with arr[n-1-i]. Count distinct pair sums in a set; averages are distinct exactly when sums are.
hints: If you sort the experience values, which two developers form the first pair? The second?
After sorting, pair i pairs arr[i] with arr[n-1-i]. You only need distinct averages, and (a+b)/2 is distinct iff a+b is, so store integer sums and avoid floating point.
Sort in O(n log n), move two pointers inward adding arr[i] + arr[j] to a set, return the set's size.
pitfalls: Storing averages as floats invites precision bugs; compare integer sums instead.
Equal values (e.g. all ones) give one distinct value, not n/2.
Pairing is decided by values, not by original positions; do not pair index 0 with index n-1 of the unsorted array.
